milestone: V8.1 Frontend UI/UX Hardcode & Quality Audit

method.deterministic_scan: native Python regex scan over frontend source
method.manual_review: architecture, UX state, accessibility and ownership review
method.rule: raw literals are leads, not automatic refactor targets

findings.title: Raw color cluster bypasses semantic tokens
findings.problem: The largest view stylesheet contains hundreds of direct hex/rgba values; repeated values are not consistently expressed through semantic tokens.
findings.why: Theme changes, contrast review and status consistency require editing many selectors and can drift.
findings.solution: Create a measured color inventory, map repeated values to existing tokens in styles/tokens.css or packages/brand, then migrate one semantic family at a time.
acceptance: Repeated semantic colors have one owner
No visual regression in V4/V5/V6 browser suites
Axe contrast remains green

findings.title: Repeated spacing and dimensions lack an explicit scale
findings.problem: Common values such as 8px, 10px, 12px and 18px recur hundreds of times beside one-off values such as 17px, 19px and 23px.
findings.why: The codebase cannot distinguish intentional component dimensions from accidental rhythm drift.
findings.solution: Define a spacing and control-size scale, then migrate repeated clusters with component-level review rather than global search/replace.
acceptance: Duplicate clusters are mapped to token names
One-off values have an explicit invariant comment or are removed
Responsive smoke remains green

findings.title: Z-index values are not centrally owned
findings.problem: Stacking values are distributed across reset, shell, component and view styles.
findings.why: New dialogs, inspectors and toasts can accidentally render below or above the wrong layer.
findings.solution: Create a documented layer scale for base, sticky, popover, modal, toast and critical overlay; replace only values proven equivalent.
acceptance: Every stacking context maps to a named layer
Popover/modal/toast order is tested
No arbitrary 9999 values remain without rationale

findings.title: Breakpoints are duplicated across CSS layers
findings.problem: The same 760px breakpoint is declared in multiple files while 940px and 1180px are locally owned.
findings.why: A responsive change can update one layer while leaving shell or view behavior inconsistent.
findings.solution: Define shared breakpoint custom properties/documentation and keep component-specific container queries local where semantically required.
acceptance: Breakpoint ownership is documented
Mobile/tablet/desktop states are verified at declared widths
No duplicated global breakpoint definitions remain

findings.title: API paths are embedded in clients and runtime helpers
findings.problem: Route strings and API version paths are spread through client methods.
findings.why: API version changes, test transport substitution and same-origin/remote deployment rules require multi-file edits.
findings.solution: Keep endpoint ownership in the API client boundary with typed route builders and environment base URL configuration; do not move canonical server paths into UI components.
findings.dependencies: API contract tests; server route registry
acceptance: UI contains no endpoint literals
Client tests cover every route builder
Same-origin and configured-base-url tests pass

findings.title: Navigation and domain metadata are split across registries
findings.problem: Domain labels, icons, aliases, object ownership and renderers are defined in separate structures.
findings.why: A new domain can become routable but lack a renderer, mobile entry or canonical object mapping.
findings.solution: Define one typed canonical domain manifest and derive aliases/renderers/navigation metadata with explicit capability filters.
acceptance: One manifest owns domain id/label/icon/route/renderer
Deep links and aliases round-trip
Unknown domains fail to a documented fallback

findings.title: Runtime mock data is mixed with initial production shell state
findings.problem: Demo users, missions, agents, approvals, artifacts and telemetry are embedded in the runtime initial state.
findings.why: Preview fixtures can be mistaken for canonical backend state and can leak into production behavior when backend data is unavailable.
findings.solution: Split explicit test/demo fixtures from production defaults and make fallback provenance visible; retain deterministic fixtures only in harnesses.
findings.dependencies: offline shell contract; browser fixtures; backend reconciliation
acceptance: Production boot has no fake consequential records
Test harness opts into fixtures explicitly
Unavailable backend renders honest empty/degraded state

findings.title: Status strings and presentation mappings are distributed
findings.problem: The same lifecycle values are compared and styled in multiple local maps and ternaries.
findings.why: A new or renamed state can render with no label, wrong color or incorrect action affordance.
findings.solution: Introduce schema-derived status definitions containing allowed transitions, label, icon, tone and accessibility text; consume it from domain and UI layers.
findings.dependencies: journey state machines; existing V6/V7 invariants
acceptance: All status consumers use canonical definitions
Unknown status renders safe fallback
Transition and presentation tests cover every status

findings.title: Currency and number formatting is locally formatted
findings.problem: Amounts use local toFixed/euro formatting rather than one domain formatter.
findings.why: Currency, locale, cents precision and negative/large-value behavior can diverge between receipts and lists.
findings.solution: Use the V7.4 integer-cent formatter at a shared boundary with explicit currency and locale inputs.
acceptance: All money displays use one formatter
Integer-cent precision is preserved
Locale/currency tests cover EUR and fallback

findings.title: Direct localStorage ownership in bootstrap
findings.problem: Storage key and persistence behavior are owned directly by the bootstrap module.
findings.why: Schema versioning, migration, reset and test isolation are difficult when storage is accessed from render/runtime code.
findings.solution: Create a versioned storage adapter with key constants, migration and failure handling; keep bootstrap dependent on the adapter only.
acceptance: No direct storage access outside adapter
Old schema migration is tested
Storage failures degrade without losing current UI state

findings.title: Inline runtime styles bypass component tokens
findings.problem: Dynamic style attributes mix layout/runtime values with presentation rules.
findings.why: They are harder to audit, can bypass responsive CSS and often encode layout assumptions.
findings.solution: Keep only measured runtime variables inline; move static presentation to classes or component tokens and document legitimate dynamic values.
acceptance: Each remaining inline style has runtime justification
Static styles use canonical classes
No accessibility or visual regression

findings.title: Accessibility state coverage is not represented as a shared contract
findings.problem: Automated checks cover current surfaces, but loading/empty/forbidden/degraded and focus restoration contracts are distributed.
findings.why: Axe success does not prove keyboard recovery or truthful state semantics across all page states.
findings.solution: Create a page/component state matrix and add deterministic keyboard/focus assertions for each primary surface.
acceptance: Every central page has loading/empty/error/offline/degraded/forbidden coverage
Keyboard path and focus restoration are tested
Axe and manual evidence are recorded

findings.title: Hardcoded UI copy is embedded in render functions
findings.problem: Labels, empty states, error text and status copy are written directly beside rendering logic.
findings.why: Terminology, localization and content review require code edits and can drift across surfaces.
findings.solution: Create a small semantic copy catalog for shared terms/statuses/errors; keep object-specific titles runtime-owned.
acceptance: Repeated UX terms have one owner
User/runtime content is not incorrectly catalogued
Copy tests cover labels and fallback states

findings.title: State booleans permit invalid combinations
findings.problem: Multiple independent booleans represent mutually exclusive surfaces, focus and runtime modes.
findings.why: Impossible combinations can produce overlapping artifact, approval, inspector and replay surfaces.
findings.solution: Model major surface ownership as discriminated state modes while retaining independent user preferences only where valid.
findings.dependencies: render scheduler; visual QA; existing interaction tests
acceptance: Invalid surface combinations are unrepresentable or rejected
Existing Chat/Work/Space flows remain unchanged
State transition tests cover open/close/recovery

findings.title: Backend response assumptions lack a single validation boundary
findings.problem: Consumers read nested response fields directly and each layer supplies partial fallback behavior.
findings.why: Contract drift can produce plausible but incomplete UI state and hide data loss behind defaults.
findings.solution: Validate/normalize server payloads once at the API boundary with explicit degraded coverage semantics.
acceptance: Malformed payloads fail closed or become explicit degraded state
Canonical owner/provenance is preserved
Representative producers and consumers are tested

findings.title: Destructive action protection is not one shared primitive
findings.problem: Approval, deny, takeover, cancel and upstream decisions have separate interaction paths.
findings.why: Confirmation, double-submit, loading and recovery semantics can diverge for consequential actions.
findings.solution: Define a canonical consequential-action state machine and shared action primitive; keep authority execution in the owner adapter.
findings.dependencies: authority audit; API contracts; existing approval tests
acceptance: Every destructive action has pending/confirmed/failed/retry states
Duplicate submit is blocked or idempotent
No UI state implies authority success before readback

findings.title: Duplicate component primitives and local variants need consolidation review
findings.problem: Buttons, rows, notices, agent cards, approval rows and surface sections have overlapping local markup/style variants.
findings.why: Fixes for focus, touch targets and semantic states must be repeated and can drift.
findings.solution: Build a consumer matrix first; consolidate only exact semantic duplicates into existing first-party primitives.
acceptance: Candidates have consumer and behavior evidence
Shared primitive preserves all required variants
No abstraction created for one-off semantics

findings.title: Dead/legacy markers require classification before cleanup
findings.problem: The raw marker scan returns many matches, including legitimate words such as temporary CSS values and comments.
findings.why: Blind deletion would remove intentional notes; leaving all markers hides real debt.
findings.solution: Parse markers with context, classify intentional vs actionable, and convert actionable items into owned backlog TODOs.
acceptance: Every marker is classified
Actionable markers have a TODO item or fix
No broad regex-only cleanup

findings.title: Responsive audit needs explicit narrow/tablet/wide evidence
findings.problem: Current automated coverage is strong for selected desktop/mobile flows but not a full component state matrix across narrow mobile, tablet and ultrawide.
findings.why: Clipping, density and hidden actions can remain unobserved outside the smoke viewport set.
findings.solution: Add a declared viewport matrix and capture the critical Control, Agents, Output, Space and replay states at each width.
findings.dependencies: FIN visual QA; browser smoke harness
acceptance: No horizontal overflow or clipped primary actions
Evidence is tied to exact revision

findings.title: Canonical ownership is undocumented for several frontend constants
findings.problem: Token, domain, runtime fixture and endpoint ownership exists but is not declared in one audit-readable contract.
findings.why: Future slices can move values to a constants file without improving ownership or can duplicate canonical definitions.
findings.solution: Add an ownership map to the audit artifact and require each new shared value to name its owner category.
acceptance: Every P0/P1 finding names owner and consumers
Ownership map is machine-readable
New audit rerun detects drift
